Asserts that the iterator returns exactly the {@code expectedLines}, in order, via {@link LineIterator#nextLine()}, and that it is exhausted afterwards. The iterator is always closed, even if an assertion fails. @param expectedLines the lines the iterator is expected to yield. @param iterator the iterator under test.

Writes a file with the given number of lines, then iterates over it verifying that every line is returned in order, that {@link LineIterator#remove()} is unsupported, and that the iterator throws once exhausted. @param lineCount the number of lines to create in the test file. @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs while creating the file.
Once every line has been consumed, both accessors must signal exhaustion.
Read a single line, leaving more lines available.
Closing early must make the iterator behave as exhausted.
close() is idempotent and the iterator stays exhausted.

Iterates over a {@link LineIterator} whose {@code isValidLine} accepts only lines whose trailing digit {@code d} satisfies {@code d % 3 != 1}. For lines {@code "LINE 0".."LINE 8"} this filters out the lines ending in 1, 4 and 7, leaving 6 of the 9 lines. @param expectedLines all lines present in the source (the unfiltered set of 9 lines). @param reader the reader to iterate over. @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs.
Inspect the trailing digit of e.g. "LINE 7"; reject lines where digit % 3 == 1.
Skip over the filtered-out line (the one whose digit % 3 == 1).
Once every valid line has been consumed, both accessors must signal exhaustion.
A reader that always fails on readLine() so hasNext() surfaces the I/O error.
